subject: Hex OS shell: consider q as an alias for quit, wired to the exit branch not SYNONYMS
description:
Raised by me and ruled on by Nancy during the round-4 review; deliberately NOT built, because the tree was frozen for her review and because the wiring is not what I assumed.

MY ASSUMPTION WAS WRONG. I described it as 'one line in SYNONYMS'. Nancy checked: SYNONYMS entries route through the 'X is not a command here. Try Y' branch, which is the WRONG answer for quit. That branch would tell a student to 'try' something, when the honest answer for exit/quit is that there is nothing to exit because the shell is a page and not a session. q must land in the acctVerb === 'exit' || acctVerb === 'quit' check, or be normalised into accountVocab, not dropped into SYNONYMS.

WHY IT IS DEFENSIBLE AT ALL: the s/r precedent does not forbid it. s and r are blocked from FUZZY-matching several real commands with unearned confidence. h and ? are already curated single-character EXACT aliases in the same file with no length floor, because an exact 1:1 mapping is not a guess. q would use the h mechanism, not the s/r one.

WHY IT MIGHT STILL BE WRONG: q is muscle memory from vim, less and man, where it exits the PROGRAM. Here it would explain that there is nothing to exit. That is arguably the most useful possible answer for that keystroke, but it is worth one operator sentence before adding a durable alias.

DO NOT loosen the account-pool distance bound to catch 'sta' -> 'start'. Nancy measured it: editDistance('sta','cat') is also 2, so widening to distance 2 makes sta ambiguous between start and cat and it still fails to resolve, just via ambiguity instead of distance. That is the same collision shape found twice already this session, relocated one level down.
